		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Business Description and Basis of Presentation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;MWI Veterinary Supply, Inc. is a leading distributor of animal health products to veterinarians in the United States and United Kingdom. We sell our products </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">primarily </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">to veterinarians in both the companion and production animal markets. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">As of September 30, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">e operate</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">thir</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">teen</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> distribution centers located across the United States and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> distribution center in the United Kingdom.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">2.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Principles of Consolidation</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; The accompanying consolidated financial statements consist of MWI&nbsp;Veterinary Supply,&nbsp;Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, collectively referred to herein as &#x201C;MWI&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company.&#x201D; All intercompany transactions have been eliminated.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use the equity method of accounting for our investments in entities in which we have significant influence; generally this represents an ownership interest between 20% and 50%. Our share of income or loss from these investments is reported as increases or decreases in the respective investment with a corresponding amount reported as other income</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">/(expense).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Basis of Accounting and Use of Estimates </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared on the accrual basis of accounting using accounting principles generally accepted in the United States. In preparing financial information, we use certain estimates and assumptions that may affect the reported amounts and disclosures. Some of these estimates require difficult, subjective and complex judgments about matters that are inherently uncertain. As a result, actual results could differ from these estimates. Estimates are used when accounting for allowance for doubtful accounts, customer incentives, vendor rebates, inventories, goodwill and intangible assets, income taxes</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> contingencies. The estimates of fair value of assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities as of the balance sheet date and reported amounts of revenue and expenses for the periods are based on assumptions that we believe to be reasonable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Segment Information</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; We are a distributor of animal health products to veterinarians. Our financial results are disclosed as </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> reportable segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;We identified </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> operating segments based on geographic areas but aggregate based on applicable accounting standards.&nbsp;&nbsp;We determined that the two operating segments have similar operating margins and are expected to maintain this similarity into the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, our products, customers, operations, delivery to market and regulatory environments are all similar in nature.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Foreign Currency Translation</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; For our international operations, local currencies have been determined to be the functional currencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;We translate functional currency assets and liabilities to their U.S. dollar equivalents at rates in effect at the balance sheet date and record these translation adjustments in Stockholders&#x2019; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">E</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">quity &#x2013; Accumulated </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">O</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ther </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">omprehensive </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">I</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ncome/(</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">L</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">oss).&nbsp;&nbsp;We translate functional currency statement of income amounts to their U.S. dollar equivalents at average rates for the period. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Other Comprehensive Income</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Comprehensive income includes cumulative foreign currency translation adjustments and actuarial adjustments on pension valuation. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">At September 30, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">accumulated other comprehensive income is comprised of actuarial adjustment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, net of tax,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">($66)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, and foreign currency translation adjustments of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,984</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenue Recognition </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We sell products we source from vendors to our customers through either a &#x201C;buy/sell&#x201D; transaction or an agency relationship with our vendors. In a &#x201C;buy/sell&#x201D; transaction, we purchase or take inventory of </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">50</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 2pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">products from the vendor. When a customer places an order with us, we pick, pack, ship and invoice the customer for the order. We recognize revenue from &#x201C;buy/sell&#x201D; transactions as product sales when the product is delivered to the customer. We accept product returns from our customers. We estimate returns based on historical experience and recognize these estimated returns as a reduction of product sales. Product returns have not been significant to our financial statements. We record revenues net of sales tax.&nbsp;&nbsp;In an agency relationship, we generally do not purchase and take inventory of products from vendors. We receive an order from a customer, then transmit the order to the vendor, who picks, packs and ships the order to the customer. In some cases, the vendor invoices and collects payment from the customer, while in other cases we invoice and collect payment from the customer on behalf of the vendor. We receive a commission payment for soliciting the order from the customer and for providing other customer service activities. Commissions are recognized when the services upon which the commissions are based are complete. Gross billings from agency contracts were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$349,006</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$332,343</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$371,024</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively, and generated commission revenue of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$18,851</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$16,979</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$20,655</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Cost of Product Sales and Vendor Rebates</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Cost of product sales consist of our inventory product cost, including shipping costs to and from our distribution centers. Costs of fulfillment are included in selling, general and administrative costs. Vendor rebates are recorded based on the terms of the contracts or programs with each vendor. We receive quarterly, semi-annual and annual performance-based rebates from third-party vendors based upon attainment of certain sales and/or purchase goals. Sales rebates are classified in the accompanying consolidated statements of income as a reduction to cost of product sales at the time the sales performance measures are achieved. Purchase rebates are measured against inventory purchases from the vendors and are classified as a reduction of inventory until the product is sold. When the inventory is sold and purchase measures are achieved, purchase rebates are recognized as a reduction to cost of product sales.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Historically, actual results have not significantly deviated from those determined using the estimates described above. We expect that our estimates in the future will continue to be reasonable as our rebates are based on specific vendor program goals and are principally recorded upon achievement of sales or purchase performance measures. Vendors may change or eliminate rebate programs from year to year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Customer Incentives </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; Customer incentives are accrued based on the terms of the contracts with each customer. These incentive programs provide that the customer receive an incentive based on their product purchases or attainment of performance goals. Incentives are estimated based on the specific terms in each agreement, historical experience and product growth rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Incentives are recognized as a reduction to product sales.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; Cash equivalents consist of highly liquid investments with a maturity of three months or less from the date of purchase. Our banking arrangements allow us to fund outstanding checks when presented to the financial institution for payment. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">In</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">ventories </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; Inventories, consisting of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">pharmaceuticals, vaccines, parasiticides, diagnostics, micro feed ingredients, capital equipment and technology, supplies and nutritional products</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, are stated at the lower of cost (on a moving-average basis) or market.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and Intangible Assets </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014; We recognize the excess purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination as goodwill on the consolidated balance sheet. We perform an annual impairment test on goodwill as of September 30th each year.&nbsp;&nbsp;We calculate the fair value of each reporting unit using</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> both an income approach and a market approach,&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and compare the fair value to its book value.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have concluded that there was no impairment during the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011. Impairment tests will continue to be performed at least annually and more frequently if circumstances indicate a possible impairment.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Identifiable intangible assets primarily include customer relationships, trademarks and patents, technology and covenants not to compete and are amortized, as necessary, over their useful lives or contractual term which range from 1-20 years.&nbsp;&nbsp;We review </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">both indefinite-lived and definite-lived </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">identifiable intangible assets at least annually for impairment or when events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;No impairments were identified during the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Other Assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Included in other assets are our equity method investments and investments in entities accounted for under the cost method of accounting, which includes an investment in Cubex of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$4,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. We periodically evaluate these investments for other-than-temporary impairment using both qualitative and quantitative criteria, or when indicators of impairment are noted. In the event an investment is deemed to be other-than-temporarily impaired, we would recognize the loss component in the consolidated statements of income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other assets also consist of debt issuance costs that are being amortized over the term of the related debt.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Earnings Per Common Share</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Basic earnings per common share is calculated based on the weighted-average number of outstanding common shares during the applicable period. Diluted earnings per common share is based on the weighted-average number of outstanding common shares plus the weighted-average number of potential outstanding common shares. Potential common shares that would increase earnings per share amounts are antidilutive and are, therefore, excluded from the earnings per common share computations. Earnings per common share is computed separately for each period presented.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Income Taxes</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method. Deferred income taxes are recognized to provide for temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax basis of assets and liabilities. Deferred taxes are measured using enacted tax rates in effect during the years in which the temporary differences are expected to reverse.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Concentrations of Risk</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Our financial instruments that are exposed to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of our receivables. Our customers are geographically dispersed throughout the United States and United Kingdom. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In the United Kingdom, we rely on a smaller number of relatively larger customers than does our business in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;These customers in the aggregate accounted fo</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">r &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">14.5%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">18.1%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of our consolidated accounts receivable balance as of September 30, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively, and one significant customer accounted for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.6%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7.6%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of our consolidated accounts receivable balance as of September 30, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We routinely assess the financial strength of our cu</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">stomers and review their credit history before extending credit. In addition, we establish an allowance for doubtful accounts based upon factors surrounding the credit risk of specific customers, historical trends and other information.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Advertising</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x2014; Advertising costs are expensed when incurred and are included as part of selling, general and administrative expenses. Advertising costs were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">165</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,203</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$723</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Recently Issued and New Accounting Pronouncements&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In January 2013, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) No. 2013-01, Clarifying the Scope of Disclosures about Offsetting Assets and Liabilities, which includes bifurcated embedded derivatives, repurchase agreements and reverse repurchase agreements, and securities borrowing and securities lending arrangements that are either offset on the balance sheet </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">or subject to an enforceable master netting arrangement or similar agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;This guidance is effective for our fiscal year beginning October 1, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not believe that the adoption of this guidance will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In February 2013, the FASB issued ASU No. 2013-02, Reporting of Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income, which provides additional disclosure requirements for items reclassified out of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">accumulated other comprehensive income</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;This guidance is effective for our fiscal year beginning October 1, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not believe that the adoption of this guidance will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">3.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Business Acquisitions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">On </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">March 21, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, MWI Co. purchased substantially all of the assets of Nelson Laboratories Limited Partnership (&#x201C;Nelson&#x201D;) for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$7,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> in cash. Nelson was a distributor of animal health products to over </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1,100</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> veterinary practices, primarily in the Midwestern United States. This acquisition allows us to better serve our customers in this region. An intangible asset representing customer relationships acquired in the acquisition has an estimated useful life of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years. The amount recorded in goodwill is deductible for tax purposes over </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">15</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">On </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">October 31, 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, MWI Co. purchased substantially all of the assets of Micro Beef Technologies, Ltd. (&#x201C;Micro&#x201D;) for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$60,878</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, including </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$53,400</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> in cash and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">94,359</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> shares of common stock valued at </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$7,158</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, which is the fair value of the common stock as of the date of acquisition and a working capital adjustment of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$320</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">. The $53,400 paid in cash as consideration of Micro was funded with borrowings under our Credit Agreement (as defined in Note 7) as then in effect. Micro is a value-added distributor to the production animal market, including the distribution of micro feed ingredients, pharmaceuticals, vaccines, parasiticides, supplies and other animal health products. Micro also is a leading innovator of proprietary, computerized management systems for the production animal market. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We incurred </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,104</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> of direct acquisition-related and integration expenses.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">The intangible assets acquired in the acquisition include technology, customer relationships, trade name and covenant not to compete. The useful life of the amortizing intangible assets ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">17</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years. Trade name is a non-amortizing intangible asset. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Goodwill is calculated as the excess of the consideration transferred over the net assets recognized and represents the future economic benefits arising from other assets acquired that could not be individually identified and separa</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">tely recognized. The goodwill recorded as part of the acquisition of Micro includes the expected synergies that we believed would result from this acquisition.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">The amount recorded in goodwill is deductible for tax purposes over 15 years. The f</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">air values assigned to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based on management's estimates and assumptions as well as other information compiled by management, including valuations that utilize customary valuation procedures and techniques. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">On </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, MWI Co. purchased substantially all of the assets of Prescription Containers, Inc. (&#x201C;PCI Animal Health&#x201D;), for a net purchase price of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$17,107</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, after consideration of post-closing adjustments.&nbsp;&nbsp;PCI Animal Health was a distributor of companion animal health products to veterinary practices, primarily in the Northeastern United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The intangible asset acquired in the acquisition is for customer relationships and has a useful life of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount recorded in goodwill is expected to be deductible for tax purposes over </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">15</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years. The fair values assigned to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based on management's estimates and assumptions, as well as other information compiled by management, including valuations that utilize customary valuation procedures and techniques. We adjusted those valuations during the nine months ended September 30, 2013 as a result of further review of these estimates and assumptions. The fair value assigned to the purchased intangible related to customer relationships decreased by </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,190</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> with a corresponding adjustment to the carrying value of goodwill. The related impact on amortization recognized from that date is insignificant to the consolidated statements of income.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">The following table summarizes the fair values of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at the date of each acquisition, which may be adjusted during the measurement period as defined in Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) 805. These purchase price allocations are based on a combination of valuations and analyses. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;">Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;&#x2014; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">MWI Co. as borrower, is party to a Credit Agreement dated December 13, 2006, as amended </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">(the &#x201C;Credit Agreement&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, by and among MWI Co., MWI, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Memorial Pet Care, Inc. and Bank of America, N.A. and Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. as lenders (collectively, the &#x201C;Lenders&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Agreement allows for an aggregate revolving commitment of the Lenders of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$150,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and a maturity date of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">November 1, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Credit Agreement, the margin on variable interest rate borrowings ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.95%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The commitment fee under the Credit Agreement ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.15%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.25%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> depending on the funded debt to EBITDA </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The variable interest rate is equal to the Daily LIBOR Floating Rate or the LIBOR 1-month, 2-month, 3-month or 6-month fixed rate (at MWI Co.&#x2019;s option) plus the margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Agreement contains financial covenants, including a fixed charge ratio and a funded debt to EBITDA ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;We were in compliance with all of the covenants as of September 30, 2013 and 2012.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;">Sterling Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> On March 15, 2013, Centaur entered into a First Amendment (the &#x201C;Amendment&#x201D;) to the unsecured revolving line of credit facility (the &#x201C;Sterling Revolving Credit Facility&#x201D;) dated November 5, 2010 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. London Branch.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Amendment increases the maximum loan amount of the Sterling Revolving Credit Facility to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#xA3;20,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, an increase of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#xA3;7,500</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, and extends the term of the facility to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">November 1, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">. Interest is based on LIBOR for the applicable interest period plus an applicable margin of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.95%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, and the commitment fee ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.15%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0.25%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, depending on our funded debt to EBITDA ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The facility contains a financial covenant requiring Centaur to maintain a minimum tangible net worth of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#xA3;5,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September 30, 2013 and 2012, Centaur was in compliance with the covenant. Our outstanding balance on the Sterling Revolving Credit Facility at September 30, 2013 was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#xA3;1,550</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, or </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$2,501</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> using the exchange rate on September 30, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate for the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">S</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">terling </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">R</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">evolving </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">redit </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">F</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">acility was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1.44%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> as of September 30, 2013.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Also on March 15, 2013, Centaur entered into an uncommitted overdraft facility (the &#x201C;Overdraft Facility&#x201D;) with Wells Fargo. The Overdraft Facility allows Centaur to borrow an additional </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xA3;10,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to fund short term normal trading cycle fluctuations. The Overdraft Facility will expire on November 1, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest on the borrowing under the Overdraft Facility is the same as the terms under the Amendment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;text-indent:20.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">8.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Common Stock and Stock-Based Awards </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">2002 Stock Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We had a 2002 Stock Plan (the &#x201C;2002 Plan&#x201D;) to provide our directors, executives and other key employees with additional incentives by allowing them to acquire an ownership interest in us and, as a result, encouraging them to contribute to our success. All options that were granted under this plan have been exercised and there are no additional shares available for issuance under the 2002 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">2005 Stock Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We have a 2005 Stock-Based Award and Incentive Compensation Plan (the &#x201C;2005 Plan&#x201D;), under which we may offer restricted shares of our common stock and grant options to purchase shares of our common stock to selected employees and non-employee directors. The purpose of the 2005 Plan is to promote our long-term financial success by attracting, retaining and rewarding eligible participants. At September 30, 2013 and 2012 we had </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">815,260</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">865,917</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> shares, respectively, of our common stock available for issuance under the 2005 Plan.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">The 2005 Plan permits us to grant stock options (both incentive stock options and non</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#8209;qualified stock options), restricted stock and deferred stock. The compensation committee will determine the number and type of stock-based awards to each participant, the exercise price of each award, the duration of the award (not to exceed </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years), vesting provisions and all other terms and conditions of such award in individual award agreements. The 2005 Plan provides for the cancellation of all unvested awards upon termination of employment with us, unless determined otherwise by the compensation committee at the time awards are granted.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">As of September 30, 2013, total unrecognized stock based compensation expense related to nonvested awards was approximately $15,911 before income taxes, which is expected to be recognized over the remaining term of the awards which range from 1 to 5 years.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013 and 2012, we recognized $3,553 and $3,569, respectively, in compensation expense related to common stock awards.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The total fair value of shares vested during the years ended September 3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0, 2013, 2012, and 2011, was $6,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">38</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, $4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">08</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, and $1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">00</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">2008 Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The 2008 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#x201C;ESPP&#x201D;) allows substantially all employees to purchase shares of our common stock at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">95%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the fair market value on the date of purchase.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase date is the last trading date of the purchase period, which begins in March, June, September and December.&nbsp;&nbsp;Employees accumulate amounts through payroll deductions during the purchase period of between </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> but no more than </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$20</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;An employee is allowed to purchase a maximum of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">200</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares per purchase period.&nbsp;&nbsp;We issued </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5,396</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">6,859</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares of our common stock under the ESPP during fiscal years ended September 30, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:20.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In general, it is the practice and intention of the Company to reinvest the earnings of its non-U.S. subsidiaries in those operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September 30, 2013, the Company has not made a provision for U.S. income or additional foreign withholding taxes on the excess of the amount for financial reporting over the tax basis of investments in foreign subsidiaries that are essentially permanent in duration.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, such amounts become subject to U.S. taxation upon the remittance of dividends and under certain other circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is not practicable to estimate the amount of deferred tax liability related to investments in foreign subsidiaries because of the complexities of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the hypothetical calculation.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">For the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, the amount included in our income tax expense for tax-related interest and penalties was not significant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$23</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> unrecognized tax benefits as of September 30, 2011, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$15</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> would have impacted our effective rate, if recognized. 		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">13.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Related Party Transactions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">MWI Co., our subsidiary, holds a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> membership interest in Feeders&#x2019; Advantage that is accounted for as an investment using the equity method. Sales of products to Feeders&#x2019; Advantage, which are at our cost, were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">68,355</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$61,873</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$55,185</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. MWI Co. charged Feeders&#x2019; Advantage for certain operating and administrative services of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1,079</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,008</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$919</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. Our President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors are each members of the board of managers of Feeders&#x2019; Advantage.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">MWI Co. allows Feeders&#x2019; Advantage to use its cash management system to finance its day-to-day operations. At any given time, the outstanding position used in the cash management system may be a receivable or payable depending on the cash activity.&nbsp;&nbsp;A receivable balance bears interest at the prime rate. The interest due on the outstanding receivable is calculated and charged to Feeders&#x2019; Advantage on the last day of each month. Conversely, to the extent MWI Co. has a payable balance due to Feeders&#x2019; Advantage, the payable balance accrues interest in favor of Feeders&#x2019; Advantage at the average federal funds rates in effect for that month.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As of September 30, 2013 MWI Co. had a payable balance to Feeders&#x2019; Advantage of </font><font style="display: inline;">$777</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of September 30</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2012 MWI Co. had a receivable balance from Feeders' Advantage of </font><font style="display: inline;">$6</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">14.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Employee Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We have a multi-employer defined contribution profit sharing plan with a 401(k)&nbsp;arrangement for employees in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;To become eligible for the profit sharing portion of the plan, an employee must complete </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">two</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> years of service and attain the age of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">twenty-one</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">. Participation is automatic beginning the following January or July. To become eligible for the 401(k) portion of the plan, the employee must complete </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">-months of service and attain the age of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">twenty-one</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Both portions of the plan allow for employer contributions. We are required to match </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> of the employee&#x2019;s contribution to the 401(k)&nbsp;portion of the plan up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">6%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> of the employee&#x2019;s salary. Our matching contributions for the 401(k)&nbsp;portion of the plan were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$2,122</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,871</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,464</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. Employee&#x2019;s contributions are fully vested immediately while employer contributions vest over a five-year period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">62</font>

		</p>

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Contributions to the profit sharing portion of the Plans are discretionary, ranging from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">0%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">3%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, and are approved by our board of directors. Total profit sharing expense for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011 were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,997</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,847</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$1,516</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, respectively. Employer contributions are fully vested immediately.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Centaur sponsors a defined contribution plan for all other staff not participating in the defined benefit plan described below. The contributions made by the employer over the period are detailed below. Contributions are currently payable at a minimum of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">3%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> up to a maximum of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">6%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> of eligible pay if matched by employee.&nbsp;&nbsp;The matching contribution for the plan was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$257</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$250</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">$269</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> for the fiscal years ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">September 30, 2013, 2012 and 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#x2003;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Current fair value accounting guidance includes a hierarchy that is intended to increase consistency and comparability in fair value measurements and disclosures.&nbsp;&nbsp;This hierarchy prioritizes inputs to valuation techniques based on observable and unobservable data.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance categorizes these inputs used in measuring fair value into three levels which include the following:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width: 100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td align="left" valign="top" style="width: 36.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 1 &#x2013; observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width: 100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td align="left" valign="top" style="width: 36.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 2 &#x2013; inputs, other than quoted prices, that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.&nbsp;&nbsp;These include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets and quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active; and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width: 100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td align="left" valign="top" style="width: 36.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 18pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 3 &#x2013; unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of September 30, 2013 and 2012, financial instruments include cash and cash equivalents, receivables and accounts payable, and the fair values approximate book values due to their short maturities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our revolving credit facilit</font><font style="display: inline;">ies</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the United States and in the United Kingdom were amended in the recent past and are based on market conditions such as LIBOR.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because these credit facilities include interest rates based on current market conditions</font><font style="display: inline;"> (Level 1 inputs)</font><font style="display: inline;">, we believe that the estimated fair value of our debt was materially the same as our carrying value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 10pt;line-height:100%;text-indent:-10pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt">

The cash purchase price was fund</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ed with borrowings by the Company under its existing Credit Agreement. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">IVESCO engaged in the distribution and sale of animal health</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and related </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">products</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and service, logistics and technical support relating to such distribution and sale of animal health </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and related </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">products.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Management&#x2019;s annual report on internal control over financial reporting and the attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm are set forth below on this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:20pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">There were no changes in our internal controls over financial reporting that occurred during our most recently completed fiscal quarter that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">o</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">ver Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The management of MWI Veterinary Supply, Inc. and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">its </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">subsidiaries (the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) is responsible for establishing and maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting (as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f)). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">There are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any internal control, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention or overriding of controls. Accordingly, even effective internal control can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation. Further, because of changes in conditions, the effectiveness of internal control may vary over time.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2013. This assessment was based on criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting described in &#x201C;Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework,&#x201D; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Based on this assessment, management believes that, as of September 30, 2013, internal control over financial reporting was effective to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:20.15pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting has been audited by Deloitte&nbsp;&amp; Touche LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Their report is included herein.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of</font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">MWI Veterinary Supply, Inc.</font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Boise, Idaho</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of MWI Veterinary Supply, Inc. and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of September 30, 2013, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">Internal Control &#x2014; Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;"> (1992)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">o</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">ver Financial Reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&nbsp;&nbsp;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company's board of directors, management, and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Because of the inherent limitations of internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness of the internal control over financial reporting to future periods are subject to the risk that the controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2013, based on the criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;">Internal Control &#x2014; Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;"> (1992)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Dutch801 Rm BT;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated financial statements and financial statement schedule as of and for th</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">e year ended September 30, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;"> of the Company and our report dated November 27, 2013 expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements and financial statement schedule.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
